Record Class SlotIdentity

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.SlotIdentity
@Internal public record SlotIdentity(net.minecraft.world.Container container, int containerSlot) extends Record
Stable cross-menu identity for a slot: the pair of its backing Container reference and its index within that container (Slot.getContainerSlot()).

Internal plumbing. Derived from a raw vanilla Slot, this is a library-internal identity primitive; consumers address slots by Address (minted by identity, never from a live Slot). The (container, index) pair below documents the stability semantics MK relies on; it is not part of the consumer surface. For durable cross-session keying, see PersistentContainerKey.

Use case. Consumer-mod per-slot state (lock markers, annotations, palette choices — any per-slot metadata) that needs to persist across menu transitions. Vanilla creates fresh Slot instances each time a menu opens, even when the underlying storage is the same. A chest's "slot 5" is a different Slot object on every open; the backing Container reference and the slot-index-within-container are the stable coordinates.

Identity stability guarantees

Two slots have equal SlotIdentity iff they reference the same underlying container position. Concretely:
  • Player-inventory slots — the player's main inventory, hotbar, armor, and offhand slots share the same Container (Player.getInventory()) across every menu that exposes them. Survival InventoryMenu, creative ItemPickerMenu, chest ChestMenu's player-inventory portion, etc. — all expose the same 41 slot-positions under the same Inventory instance. Identity is stable across these menu transitions.
  • Block-entity-backed slots (chests, shulkers as placed blocks, hoppers, dispensers) — identity is stable while the block entity persists. Breaking and replacing the block, or unloading and reloading its chunk, produces a new block entity instance and therefore new identities.
  • Item-container slots (shulker-box contents viewed via a consumer-mod peek mechanism, bundle contents) — generally unstable. Such containers are usually ephemeral wrappers around item NBT; a fresh wrapper is constructed per observation.

Identity is session-scoped. Container references die with the JVM session. For persistence across disconnect/relog, consumer mods store their state in Fabric attachments or similar per-world persistent storage, keyed by a stable per-world identifier (player UUID + slot-in-inventory index, block position, etc.) rather than by SlotIdentity directly.

Typical consumer use

// Lock a slot on keybind press:
SlotIdentity id = SlotIdentity.of(hoveredSlot);
myLockMap.put(id, new LockState(true));

// Check later from a different menu showing the same underlying slot:
boolean locked = Optional.ofNullable(myLockMap.get(SlotIdentity.of(otherSlot)))
        .map(LockState::isLocked)
        .orElse(false);

Consumers that key data by SlotIdentity should mitigate memory retention in long-running sessions by using WeakHashMap keyed on the Container reference as the outer-level storage, with the slot index as the inner key. That pattern allows container references (and their associated state) to be GC'd when vanilla releases them (chunk unload, block break).

Why this ships as a MenuKit primitive

Phase 11 consumer-mod refactor work surfaced the cross-menu slot-state need in inventory-plus's lock-state feature. The (container, index) tuple is already vanilla's natural stable slot identity; MenuKit formalizes the abstraction so consumers don't each reinvent it.

The library ships only the identity primitive — not a registry, not a state-management service, not cross-menu enumeration helpers. Consumers manage their own state keyed by SlotIdentity; library-not-platform discipline holds.
